gaps: Breath one sorted the deaths by the pointer's own question, visible from inside or only from the morgue, and the sort came out clean along a different line: every death visible from inside had a killer that existed before anyone spoke (a category, a witness, a consentless signer, a clause with a third party), and every morgue-only death had the talks as the killer, because from inside the talks read as progress. This produced the changed question for breath two: which deaths does negotiating manufacture, and does the act of closing manufacture deaths of its own?
accepted: No line to put it on: both principals want the trade but the paying side's books have no category the payment can post to, as when a company wants to pay an open-source maintainer and has a vendor-onboarding path but no purchase that fits it, a hospital wants a device that is neither capital equipment nor a consumable, or the early Franciscans wanted bequests their rule forbade them to own until a fictive owner was invented; an outsider reads low priority, but the want is intact and the transaction has no name in the one place it must be written.

Missing witness: the closing instrument requires an attestation from a third party that nobody can produce, as a business sale that needs audited accounts from a seller who never kept auditable books, or a grain forward that needs a warehouse certificate the elevator cannot issue; not distrust between the principals, who may both believe the fact, but a form that will not accept belief, and where witness-architectures' missing witness kills the fact, this one leaves the fact standing and kills the trade.

Signer with no upside: a required consent belongs to someone who gains nothing by giving it and is blamed if it goes wrong, as a landlord asked to consent to a lease assignment, a bonding surety asked to approve a change order, or a co-heir; silence is that signer's best move and it runs on no clock, so an outsider reads bureaucratic delay while the deal dies of an asymmetry at one signature the principals cannot buy past without making the signer a party.

Third chair's clause: a term both principals would accept is forbidden or multiplied by a clause in one party's contract with someone not in the room, as a most-favoured-nation clause that propagates a grocer's discount to every other grocer, a reinsurance treaty that excludes the risk the underwriter wants to write, or a lender covenant that forbids the waiver; an outsider reads stubbornness over a small term, but the negotiator is refusing the portfolio the term would sign, and the killer sits in a chair outside the room.

Champion's single-tender want: an organization's want for a deal is held entirely in one sponsor's political capital, so when that person leaves or is reassigned the deal has no holder though the business case is untouched; an outsider reads a change of strategy, but nothing about the deal changed except who could be blamed for it, and nobody arriving cold spends their own capital on a stranger's deal.

Ratifier's other deal: the negotiator was not the principal, and the body that must ratify, a membership, a board, a spouse, a head office, had been wanting a different deal all along, so the term sheet arrives as a stranger's bargain, as when a membership votes down the tentative agreement its own leadership signed; an outsider reads bait-and-switch, but both negotiator and ratifier still want a deal, only not the same one, and the mandate was narrower than either side of the table believed.

No sentence to say it with: a principal wants the terms but has no form of words in which its own audience can hear them without hearing defeat, as a union offered under a new name the term it struck against, or a ministry offered what it had called unacceptable; an outsider reads pride, but the deal lacks an announcement rather than a price, and where impasse-inventions' face-saving fiction is the chip, this is the death when no fiction can be minted.

Report that must be acted on: a defect the seller always knew and the buyer would have priced becomes, once written in a diligence report, a record that the buyer's lender, insurer, or board is obliged to act on, as contamination under a site the seller has run for thirty years; not a hidden fact surfacing, since the fact was tacitly priced by both, but a tacit fact made a record, and an outsider reads concealment where there was only silence.

Concession-made option: a concession reveals a need or a divisibility that creates an alternative that did not exist when talks began, as a buyer whose demand for exclusivity teaches the seller that a rival would bid, or a seller whose willingness to carve out one asset teaches the buyer that the asset alone can be had elsewhere; not a hidden alternative surfacing but one manufactured by the talks, and an outsider reads the other side shopping the deal.

Price found too precisely: a deal closes inside a zone of mutual ignorance about where in the zone it sits, and when a leak or a disclosed second bid shows one side exactly how much it left on the table, that side can no longer sign in front of its own ratifier though the price still beats its alternative; not a change in value or in reservation but in the legibility of the split, and an outsider reads greed.

Cost of the last mile: closing costs accrue with every week the deal stays open, counsel, held attention, deferred decisions, an expiring rate lock, until the remaining cost to close exceeds the remaining surplus for one side though the surplus never shrank; an outsider reads lost interest, but the deal died on a curve, and by analogy a honeybee swarm that cannot reach quorum on a nest site before its stores run down dies on the same curve.

Rotting subject: the negotiation lasts longer than the subject keeps, so the thing at the end is not the thing bargained for, as a charter negotiated past the cargo's loading window, a startup whose runway ends during acquisition talks, or customers who leave a business when they hear it is for sale; distinct from parties changed, since the parties are the same and what decayed is the good.

residue.item: Deadline nobody may name: between parties who like each other, the first to name a closing date reveals need, so neither does and no force pushes the deal shut.
residue.why: Rejected for now: its cure is impasse-inventions' invented deadline, and as a death it is Cost of the last mile with nobody willing to name the curve; the signalling mechanism is real but earns its own item only if it can kill a deal whose last-mile cost is zero, and no such case was found.

residue.item: Agent's own fee: the broker paid on close wants any close and the lawyer paid hourly wants none, so the agents want a different deal than the principals.
residue.why: Rejected: a respectable agency mismatch with no new carrier; where it kills, it kills as Ratifier's other deal read from the agent's side, a mandate narrower than the table believed.

residue.item: Two clocks: each side can only sign inside a periodic window (board meeting, fiscal year, harvest) and the phases never align.
residue.why: Merged into Cost of the last mile: a phase miss is a step on the same cost curve, one cycle of accrued cost per miss; a separate item needs a case where the phases never align even at zero carrying cost, which would be a clocks-that-are-not-clocks question rather than a death.

residue.item: Market moved: the price of the asset fell during the talks and the buyer walked.
residue.why: Rejected as a nonmember: the buyer's valuation changed, so a want died rather than a wanted deal; kept as the boundary case against which Self-moving denominator is defined.

residue.item: Champion oversold: the sponsor promised the organization a larger deal than arrives, and the organization compares the term sheet to the promise rather than to its alternative.
residue.why: Merged into Ratifier's other deal: the deal the ratifier had been wanting is the one the champion described, so the carrier is the same mandate gap; the case survives there.

gate: declared modality, recognizable distinction, defensible seriation and conditional relations
limits: Authored conceptual fieldwork, not a taxonomy or a partition; a real dead deal usually has several of these carriers at once, and the list makes no claim to cover every kind.

'Both sides want' is idealized: want is taken at the reservation price at the moment of death, so deaths in which a party's valuation genuinely changed (the market moved, the subject decayed on the calendar, a real alternative that always existed came into view) are outside, as are deals one side never meant to close.

The seriation is an itinerary of where the killer was made, not a ranking of frequency, cost, or blame; its claim that visibility from inside tracks the itinerary is an authored interpretation, not a measured regularity, and map edges are conditional authored claims.

Illustrative cases (union ratification votes, most-favoured-nation propagation, stock collars, prenuptial agreements, the Franciscan ownership fiction, honeybee quorum) are simplified to expose one mechanism each and are not claims about specific histories or about bees.

Ghost closing's strong form is speculative and marked so, and the swarm in Cost of the last mile is an analogy, not a claim about bees; nothing here has been checked against a set of actual dead deals.

gaps: The changed question yielded deaths the talks manufacture (Paid in the tasting, Parties changed by talking, Retrade turns price into character) and deaths the closing act manufactures (Self-moving denominator, Ghost closing, Paper as insult); the of-sentence now names both. Applying the type strictly cut Rotting subject, admitted in breath one: calendar decay changes the want, and the half caused by the talks, customers leaving on hearing of the sale, moved into Self-moving denominator as a non-financial unit the deal moves. The territory pointer 'deal deaths' stands, the slug is kept, and the pointer's visibility question is answered by the seriation rather than by a separate axis: killers made before the talks are inspectable from inside, killers that are the talks are seen from the morgue, killers made by closing are seen from inside only by someone who has been to the morgue before.
accepted: Paid in the tasting: the negotiation delivers enough of the good that the deal is no longer needed, as an acquisition for a team's know-how whose diligence sessions transfer enough of it to build without them, or a partnership whose joint planning teaches each firm what the other knew; distinct from the concession-made option because no third party appears and the buyer's alternative is now its own hands, and an outsider reads a buyer who used the seller.

Parties changed by talking: a long negotiation changes what each party is, so the deal that fit them at the first meeting no longer fits them at the last, as a seller who learns during talks to run the business the buyer's way and no longer needs to sell, or a target's engineers who learn what the acquirer is like and leave; not cold feet, since the parties who began still want the deal they began, and those parties no longer exist.

Retrade turns price into character: a price cut delivered after the other bidders have been dismissed under exclusivity converts a price question into a question about the counterparty's honesty, which the seller cannot price and will not pay, though the retraded number still clears its reservation; an outsider reads the seller as irrational, but the seller has noticed that it is being asked to sign with someone whose next retrade it cannot see.

Self-moving denominator: the price is denominated in something the deal's own announcement moves, as a stock-for-stock merger whose announcement drops the acquirer's shares through the collar, a business whose customers leave on hearing it is for sale, or a team whose acquisition brings every member an outside offer, so the deal signed is not the deal that reaches closing; not the market moving but the deal moving its own unit, and an outsider reads bad luck in timing.

Ghost closing: the deal is lived before it is signed, shipments on a handshake, a venture run on a memorandum, so signing loses its urgency, and when the first dispute arrives there is nothing to enforce and the dispute becomes the negotiation; speculative in its strong form, that the first dispute either signs the paper or kills the deal and never neither, and an outsider reads a broken contract where there was never one.

Paper as insult: the parties have agreed and often already performed, and the request for a signed document is read as a withdrawal of trust, as when a prenuptial agreement ends the engagement it was meant to protect or a cofounder's request for a vesting schedule ends the company; both want the substance and the form kills it, an outsider reads that they never really agreed, and a standard form authored by no one is the one paper that carries no accusation.

residue.item: Rotting subject: the negotiation lasts longer than the subject keeps, so the thing at the end is not the thing bargained for, as a charter negotiated past the cargo's loading window, a startup whose runway ends during acquisition talks, or customers who leave a business when they hear it is for sale; distinct from parties changed, since the parties are the same and what decayed is the good.
residue.why: Cut on the strict type: the charter past its laycan and the startup out of runway change the good's value, so the want changes and the death is outside by the boundary claim; the talk-caused case (customers leaving on hearing of the sale) is Self-moving denominator, and nothing remained that was both calendar-caused and a wanted deal.

residue.item: Winner's curse realized: in a common-value auction the winner learns from winning that it overpaid, and walks before signing.
residue.why: Rejected as a nonmember: the want dies with the realization; Price found too precisely keeps only the case where the price still beats the side's alternative and what changed is the legibility of the split in front of a ratifier.

residue.item: Fiduciary interloper: the announced deal invites a topping bid, and the seller's board is obliged to take it though it wanted the first buyer.
residue.why: Merged into Self-moving denominator: the announcement moves the seller's set of bids exactly as it moves the acquirer's shares, the deal moving its own unit; a separate item would need the interloper to appear without the announcement, and then it is a hidden alternative surfacing, which the type excludes.

residue.item: Rumour before readiness: a leak forces the deal into the open before either side has a sentence to announce it with, and the exposure kills it.
residue.why: Unresolved seed: it splits between No sentence to say it with (no announcement exists) and Self-moving denominator (the exposure moves the unit); it earns an item only with a case where the leak kills a deal that had both a sentence and a fixed unit, and none was found in this breath.

neighbors.left: Concession-made option: a concession reveals a need or a divisibility that creates an alternative that did not exist when talks began, as a buyer whose demand for exclusivity teaches the seller that a rival would bid, or a seller whose willingness to carve out one asset teaches the buyer that the asset alone can be had elsewhere; not a hidden alternative surfacing but one manufactured by the talks, and an outsider reads the other side shopping the deal.
neighbors.right: Paid in the tasting: the negotiation delivers enough of the good that the deal is no longer needed, as an acquisition for a team's know-how whose diligence sessions transfer enough of it to build without them, or a partnership whose joint planning teaches each firm what the other knew; distinct from the concession-made option because no third party appears and the buyer's alternative is now its own hands, and an outsider reads a buyer who used the seller.
neighbors.separating_case: An acquirer's engineers sit in the target's design reviews for two months. If they leave knowing how to build the product, the target was tasted, no third party is needed, and the death is measured by what the buyer can now do alone. If instead the target's engineers leave those same reviews knowing what the acquirer pays and carry the number to the acquirer's rival, an option was made and nothing was consumed, and the death is measured by who else is now at the table. Same room, two deaths, and the remedies differ: limit what the buyer sees, or limit what the seller learns about the buyer's need.

checks.boundary_case: A buyer that walks because the market for the asset fell during the talks is out: its valuation changed, so a want died, not a wanted deal. Self-moving denominator is in on exactly that contrast, since there the price moved because the deal was spoken, not because the world moved. A counterparty that never meant to close (cooperative-masks) is out because only one side wanted it, and a deal killed by fraud is out because once the fraud is known the want is gone.
checks.form_inference: The map shows a fork the sequence conceals: from Report that must be acted on, pricing the finding leads to Retrade turns price into character and waiving it leads to Third chair's clause, and there is no branch on which the record is merely priced. It shows a loop, Retrade turns price into character ↔ Price found too precisely, where each retrade teaches the other side more precision and the loop ends in character rather than in a price. It shows an incompatibility at Missing witness → Paper as insult: the record that cures one death is the carrier of the other, so past that point no single closing form is safe and the deal needs paper from neither party. It shows a passage between levels at Third chair's clause → Ratifier's other deal, where a bilateral price becomes a question about a party's whole book and arrives at the ratifier as a different deal. And it shows a dependency, Ghost closing → Paper as insult, where performance without paper closes the signing window behind itself.
checks.target_preserved: Self-read only. Each item names one carrier of death and what an outsider misreads it as; the strange members (a trade with no category to post to, a signer whose best move is silence, a record that obliges, a number read as character, a document read as accusation, a deal that dies of being announced) are kept as mechanisms rather than softened into advice about closing faster or negotiating in good faith.

next_crossfield_opening: Paper that accuses nobody: connect Paper as insult with witness-architectures' Ledger that makes the debt and impasse-inventions' neutral holder; ask which closing instruments constitute the deal without either party having asked for them (a standard form nobody authored, a registry that records by default, an escrow that signs on performance), and whether a witness that neither party summoned can close a deal that any paper from either party would kill.

gaps: The declared type ('both principals still want, at a price both would still accept') and the second breath contradicted each other, applied selectively: Rotting subject was cut on it while Paid in the tasting, Parties changed by talking, and Concession-made option fail the same test. The criterion actually in use was endogeneity, the killer must be the deal itself (its outside arrangements, a structure inside one party, the talks, the closing act) rather than the world or the calendar; the repair went to the type, not the items, and the strict 'still clears its reservation' members stay as a sub-case rather than the rule.
accepted: Parties changed by talking: a long negotiation replaces the party the deal was fitted to, without transferring anything, as a founder who spends a year explaining the company to a buyer and discovers in the telling that she does not want to leave it, or a target's engineers who learn what the acquirer is like and resign before signing; not cold feet, since the parties who began still want the deal they began, and those parties no longer exist, and not Paid in the tasting, since nothing was consumed and the death is measured by who now sits in the chair rather than by what either side can do alone.

Signer with no upside: a required consent belongs to someone who gains nothing by giving it and is blamed if it goes wrong, as a landlord asked to consent to a lease assignment, a bonding surety asked to approve a change order, or a co-heir; silence is that signer's best move and it runs on no clock unless a deemed-consent rule has been written onto that one signature, the cure that names the killer, so an outsider reads bureaucratic delay while the deal dies of an asymmetry at one signature the principals cannot buy past without making the signer a party.

residue.item: Critic's duplication note that Signer with no upside sits beside coalition-frictions' veto queue and adds that the signer is not a coalition member and that the asymmetry (no gain from consenting, blame if it fails) rather than summed latency is what kills
residue.why: Offered as an undeclared adjacency, not as a repair; the item text was not changed and the adjacency is recorded here rather than written into the item.

residue.item: Critic's aside that in Price found too precisely → Retrade turns price into character 'its only repair is a retrade of its own' is slightly strong, since the side that learns the split can also walk or take a side letter
residue.why: The critic kept the edge because the loop claim, each turn teaching the other side more precision and ending in character, is a relation the sequence hides; the label was left as written.

limits: Type restated from 'both principals still want at a price both would still accept' to the endogeneity criterion: no change from outside in the world, the calendar, or either party's valuation; boundary_claim reconciled so talk-changed valuations are inside and the reservation-clearing members are the strict sub-case.

Edges relabeled: Report → Retrade now needs the cut to land on the headline number under exclusivity against a fact already discounted (double-counting), Report → Third chair concedes the ring-fenced instrument (escrow, specific indemnity, bought policy) as the one branch that closes and names it as the passage into impasse-inventions, and Missing witness → Paper as insult takes a party's own representation and warranty as the substitute that accuses, since the third party's book is unavailable by hypothesis. Seriation unchanged; the critic found the Tasting/Parties adjacency earned by the item repair (something transferred beside nothing transferred).
seed: The map plants three cures by re-description without noticing they form a list: the fictive owner that gives a bequest a line to post to, the new name that gives a struck-against term a sentence, and the standard form authored by no one that gives paper no author to accuse. The sharpest member the map points at but does not contain is the request that accuses nobody: a demand for paper that originates with a third party (a lender, an auditor, a registry that records by default, an escrow that signs on performance), which survives both Missing witness and Paper as insult because it is neither a party's paper nor a party's request. The list behind it is 'deaths a rename cures', with its own boundary: which of these seventeen deaths yield to re-description and which require a new party in the room.
